"""Targeted: 32-position patterns across chunks, exhaustive overlapping occurrences."""
import json, subprocess, sys, os, tempfile, random, itertools
MAIN = "/app/submission/main.py"

def canon(o): return len(json.dumps(o, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=True).encode())
d = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir="/workspace/tmp")

def run(cfg, reqs):
    p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-I", MAIN, "compile"], input=json.dumps(cfg).encode(), stdout=subprocess.PIPE)
    assert p.returncode == 0, p.stdout
    prog = os.path.join(d, "p.json"); open(prog, "wb").write(p.stdout)
    pr = subprocess.Popen([sys.executable, "-I", MAIN, "stream", prog], stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, cwd=d)
    out = []
    for r in reqs:
        pr.stdin.write(json.dumps(r).encode() + b"\n"); pr.stdin.flush()
        out.append(json.loads(pr.stdout.readline()))
    pr.stdin.close(); assert pr.wait() == 0
    return out

rnd = random.Random(11)
# one 32-position rule with tight ranges, plus a 5-position rule, plus a 1-position rule
pat = [rnd.randint(-6, 6) for _ in range(32)]
cfg = {"version": 1, "idle_timeout": 10 ** 9, "packet_limit": 10 ** 9, "prefix_width": 1,
       "rules": [
           {"id": 100, "class": 1, "priority": 10,
            "ranges": [[v, v] for v in pat]},
           {"id": 200, "class": 2, "priority": 5,
            "ranges": [[v, v] for v in pat[:5]]},
           {"id": 300, "class": 3, "priority": 1, "ranges": [[pat[0], pat[0]]]},
       ],
       "fallback": {"class": 9}}
feats = pat * 3 + [pat[0]] * 4     # 100 packets; overlapping occurrences everywhere
reqs = [{"op": "open", "flow": 1, "time": 0}]
t = 0
pk = []
for i, v in enumerate(feats):
    t = i // 7          # split across chunk boundaries mid-pattern
    pk.append({"flow": 1, "time": t, "source": 0 if v > 0 else 1, "length": abs(v) or 1})
# rebuild features from what the engine will see: feature = +len if same source as first
# first packet source determines forward; use source 0 for positive, 1 for negative
first_src = pk[0]["source"]
chunks = []
for i in range(0, len(pk), 4):
    chunks.append({"op": "chunk", "packets": pk[i:i + 4]})
reqs += chunks
reqs.append({"op": "close", "flow": 1, "time": t + 1})
out = run(cfg, reqs)

# expected features
real = []
for p in pk:
    s, L = p["source"], p["length"]
    real.append(L if s == first_src else -L)
# but if first packet's source != first_src... first_src IS pk[0]["source"], so real[0] = +len
exp_matches = []
n = 0
for i, f in enumerate(real):
    n += 1
    for rid, k in ((100, 32), (200, 5), (300, 1)):
        if n >= k and all(real[n - k + j] == pat[j] for j in range(k)):
            exp_matches.append((rid, n - k, n))
exp_matches.sort(key=lambda x: (x[1], x[0]))
got = []
for resp in out:
    for e in resp.get("events", []):
        if e["type"] == "match":
            got.append((e["rule"], e["start"], e["end"]))
got.sort(key=lambda x: (x[1], x[0]))
print("matches expected", len(exp_matches), "got", len(got), "equal:", got == exp_matches)
assert got == exp_matches, (got[:10], exp_matches[:10])
# check ordering within a single response is ascending rule id
for resp in out:
    ids = [e["rule"] for e in resp.get("events", []) if e["type"] == "match"]
    assert ids == sorted(ids), ids
closed = [e for r in out for e in r.get("events", []) if e["type"] == "closed"]
print("closed:", closed)
assert closed[0]["matches"] == len(exp_matches)
print("OK")
PYEOF
